Tailored — Brand Book 1.201 Foundations
Foundations · The reset
The category looks the same everywhere.
We will not.
× We drop
  • Purple-to-blue gradients and glowing orbs
  • Frosted-glass cards on dark mode by default
  • Sparkle icons and robot mascots standing in for “AI”
  • Inter on white, rounded 12px cards, pill buttons
  • Stock handshakes, laptops on desks
  • Slogans about “supercharging” your career
✓ We build from
  • A real trade with real tools: pattern, chalk, tape, notch, thread
  • Warm greige, espresso ink and one confident red thread
  • A custom stitched letterform nobody else owns
  • Sharp corners with deliberate notches
  • Numbers shown as measurements, not marketing
  • Arabic designed first-class, not translated after
Test for every future design decision: if it could be pasted onto any other AI product and still look right, it is wrong for Tailored.

EGP of AI compute per complete application
Beachhead: Egypt and the Gulf. English-first professionals who live on LinkedIn and Wuzzuf, read Arabic at home, and hate paying US-dollar subscriptions on local salaries.
Model: pay-per-application credit packs from 49 EGP. No lock-in. The brand must feel as fair as the pricing: generous, transparent, never pushy.
Rhythm: graduate wave Jun–Aug, layoff and restructuring wave Nov–Jan, hiring surge Jan–Mar. Brand tone shifts between hopeful and urgent.
04
Tailored — Brand Book 1.201 Foundations
Foundations · The insight
One CV,
a hundred
jobs, zero
fit.
Recruiters skim for seconds. They are not rejecting people, they are rejecting mismatch: the wrong keywords, the wrong emphasis, the right skills hidden on page two.
Job seekers know this, so they either send the same document everywhere and hope, or burn hours rewriting by hand. Existing AI tools make it worse: generic paragraphs, invented achievements, and a monthly bill.
Our insight: a good application is not written, it is tailored. Measured once, cut per job, every stitch visible and checkable.

Tailored — Brand Book 1.201 Foundations
Foundations · Positioning
For ambitious job seekers in Egypt and the Gulf who are tired of sending one CV to every job, Tailored is the made-to-measure application studio that reads each job, scores your fit honestly, and re-cuts your CV and cover letter to match — without inventing a single thread.
Unlike subscription résumé builders that spray generic AI text, we charge per application, show every change, and treat Arabic as a first language.

Tailored — Brand Book 1.201 Foundations
Foundations · Voice & tone
Plain-spoken. Precise. Warm.
Say it plainly
Short sentences. Concrete nouns. One idea per line. No jargon unless the user used it first.
Show the work
Every claim travels with a number, a reason, or a diff. If we cannot prove it we do not say it.
Be kind about the fit
A 48 is not a failure, it is information. We say what to fix, never what is wrong with them.
Dry, never silly
A little wit in empty states and success. None in errors or payments.

Tailored — Brand Book 1.202 Identity
Identity · The name
One name,
two languages,
one meaning.
Tailored — adjective: made to measure. It is also the verb we perform on every CV and cover letter.
تفصيل (tafsīl, say taf-SEEL) — in Egyptian and Gulf Arabic, tafsīl is exactly what a tailor does: cutting cloth to your measure. It also means detail. A name that says precision and craft in a single word, with no translation loss.
Rule: the Arabic name is not a transliteration of “Tailored”. It is the same idea, native to the reader. Both are always written in the brand lettering, never typed in a font.

Tailored — Brand Book 1.202 Identity
Identity · The logo explained
A pattern piece, a notch, a thread.
A — The notch
B — The T
C — The stitch
A
The notch
Tailors cut tiny triangles into the edge of every pattern piece so two pieces meet exactly where they should. Our notch is the match: your CV meeting the job. It is also the brand’s pointer, bullet, and cursor.
B
The T
A cross-bar like the shoulders of a garment on a single measured stem. Heavy, stable, symmetric: it reads as a hanger, a pattern piece, and the initial of the name. Sharp corners, no rounding.
C
The stitch
A topstitch runs inside the edge in thread red. It is the “we never invent a thread” promise: every change is visible and sewn on. At small sizes the stitch drops out and the shape stands alone.
In Arabic, the dots of تفصيل are re-cut as notches, so both scripts carry the same signature.
19
Tailored — Brand Book 1.202 Identity
Identity · Construction
Built on a
100-unit grid.
Bar88 × 28 units
Stem24 units wide, to y = 94
Notch12 wide, 8 deep, centred
Stitch5 inset · 6 on / 4.6 off · 2.6 weight
CornersSquare by default. One 26px “armhole” curve per object, top-right (top-left in Arabic).
Never redraw the mark by hand. Use the supplied vector files; stitch cadence is calculated to close evenly around the outline.
20
Tailored — Brand Book 1.202 Identity
Identity · The wordmark
Lower-case, built from straight lines
and true circles.
Custom letterforms. Eight letters drawn from one stroke (16 units) on a 60-unit x-height: bowls are perfect circles of 23-unit radius, stems are verticals. No font was used.
The i-dot is the notch. The only ornament in the word. It echoes the mark and ties the letters to the pattern-piece system.
Centre-line stitch. A running stitch (4.6 on, 4.0 off) is knocked out along every stroke’s centre-line, or sewn in thread red on the primary version.
21
Tailored — Brand Book 1.202 Identity
Identity · The Arabic wordmark
Kufi, re-cut to
share one signature.
The Arabic name is set in a geometric Kufi (Reem Kufi Bold) and then hand-modified: every dot becomes a triangular notch, pointing down above the letters and up below. The same topstitch runs inside every stroke.
  • Reads tafsīl right to left. Never letter-space or break the joins.
  • Dots are always notches. Never round dots in the logo.
  • Optical weight is matched to the Latin wordmark, not the stroke width.
Arabic monogram · ت

Tailored — Brand Book 1.204 Typography
Typography · Tailored Stitch · Anatomy
Drawn, not
chosen.
Every glyph is one monoline stroke. That makes the stitch mathematically exact: a running stitch is laid along the centre-line of each letter, so it follows curves, joins and ends without ever colliding.
Stroke16 units
x-height60 units
Ascender100 units
Bowl radius23 units, true circle
Tracking14 units (default)
Stitch4.6 on / 4.0 off, 2.2 wide
TerminalsFlat, square. No serifs.

Tailored — Brand Book 1.204 Typography
Typography · Tailored Stitch · Modes
Three settings: thread, knock-out, solid.
Thread · hero use, ≥ 56 px cap-height
Knock-out · mono, any background, ≥ 40 px
Solid · small sizes, < 40 px
Where it appears
  • The wordmark and short statements
  • Big numbers: fit scores, prices, counts
  • Section openers (≤ 4 words, lower-case)
  • Social covers and campaign lines
Where it never appears
  • Paragraphs, buttons, form labels, nav
  • Anything under 28 px cap-height
  • Upper-case (the face has no capitals)
  • Tight tracking: never below 10 units
Big number

Tailored — Brand Book 1.204 Typography
Typography · Tailored Stitch Arabic
Kufi, re-cut
by the same rules.
Arabic display text uses Reem Kufi Bold, processed with the same pipeline as the Latin: dots become notches, a topstitch runs inside each stroke. The result is a display face that is native to both scripts, not a Latin face with Arabic bolted on.
  • Statements of ≤ 5 words only
  • Never letter-spaced; never italic
  • Body Arabic always in Plex Sans Arabic

Tailored Stitch ships today as vector lettering and a build script. Commissioning a full OpenType font (caps, kerning, Arabic joining) is recommended once the identity is approved.

Tailored — Brand Book 1.203 — Colour System
Colour Don'ts
What to never do.
Never use off-palette colours
No spontaneous brand colours — not coral, not sage, not dusty rose. The palette is complete.
Never use gradients
Gradients are indecisive. The brand uses flat fields only.
Never overlay logo on pattern without container
The logo requires a solid single-colour field. Pattern backgrounds need a solid block behind the mark.
Never use THREAD as a text colour on CHALK at small sizes
THREAD on CHALK passes AA at large sizes only (≥18pt). Use INK for body text, always.
Never mix semantic and brand roles
GREEN means Strong Fit. It is not a CTA button colour. ALARM means error. It is not for urgency headlines.
Never tint or shade palette colours
Tints are from the neutral scale only. No arbitrary opacity on brand colours.
✕ No gradients
✕ Off-palette background

Tailored — Brand Book 1.205 Graphic language
Graphic language · Overview
Stitch, notch, curve.
The stitch
A dashed run of thread. It joins things, underlines things and marks the seam. Always THREAD on light and dark grounds.
The notch
The small V cut a tailor makes to line two pieces up. Our bullet, our marker, our brand signature.
The curve
The French curve and the armhole. The one soft, moving gesture in a system of straight cuts. New in version 1.2.
Everything is cut straight except the one place the body moves. That is the whole shape rule.
55
Tailored — Brand Book 1.205 Graphic language
Graphic language · Shape rule
One curve per object.
Cards, panels, buttons and images are square. Exactly one corner carries a soft armhole curve. It gives the page a lean, a direction, a little life.
  • Radius 26px for panels, 12px for buttons, 44px for hero images
  • Top-right in English, top-left in Arabic
  • Never two curves on the same side

Tailored — Brand Book 1.205 Graphic language
Graphic language · Curve motif
The French curve.
The template tailors use to draw necklines and armholes becomes our motion line: covers, section openers, empty states and loading arcs.
Use one or two sweeps per layout. Three to four parallel strokes only on covers. Always THREAD on INK, INK on CHALK.

61
Tailored — Brand Book 1.206 — Product UI
Product UI
The interface is the brand.
Precision over flair
Every pixel must earn its place. The interface communicates job intelligence — clarity is the highest form of craft.
Sharp cut, one curve
No pill-shaped blobs. One curved corner per object, like an armhole. The voice is warm and direct, like a skilled tailor advising a client.
RTL first-class
Arabic layouts are not mirrored afterthoughts. Every component is designed bidirectionally from the first commit.
Fit as north star
The fit score is the product's heartbeat. UI hierarchy always surfaces relevance first, detail second.
Stitch, not chrome
The only ornament is the stitch. No drop shadows on interactive elements, no decorative borders, no imagery in UI chrome.
Zero empty states
Every empty state is an action prompt. The product is never silent.
